text:
emma: Hi all, just joined this week. I was running a small load test locally to validate embeddings and suddenly started seeing 429s then 401s after I tried rotating a hosted key. A few quick q's: should new hires ever use hosted keys locally? Where do I get a sandbox key if so? And what's the fast path to avoid 429s while onboarding? :wave:

kai: welcome! :tada: short answers: 1) No, avoid hosted keys for day-to-day local dev. 2) Create a sandbox key in the Console (Console -> API keys -> Create sandbox key). 3) For onboarding load you can request a short-lived CI sandbox key.

leah: adding some nuance: hosted keys are for staging/prod, higher quota but sensitive. Sandbox keys are lower quota and intended for dev/test. If your Console UI only shows "Hosted" maybe SSO/role provisioning hasn't propagated; give it a minute or open a ticket.

emma: I found the sandbox key but it's throttling super fast when I loop 200 requests. Any quick mitigations while I wait for a CI key?

kai: a couple of practical patterns: 1) throttle locally with a small sleep or token-bucket limiter; 2) honor Retry-After header and do exponential backoff (jitter is helpful); 3) mock the API for unit tests and run a small integration test against the real API; 4) reduce test payload sizes (fewer tokens) or batch fewer items per request.

leah: also consider batching fewer items per request and using embeddings with lower dimension for tests. Monitor headers like X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Limit, and Retry-After to see what's hitting you.

emma: what's the recommended way to ask for a CI sandbox key? Any template?

devex-bot: Use the template below in #devex:
"Quota/key request - repo:<repo-name>, purpose:<CI|staging|pairing>, expected RPS:<n>, duration:<24h|72h|other>, contact:<your-handle>"
Example: "Quota/key request - repo:ml-evals, purpose:CI integration tests, expected RPS:5, duration:48h, contact:@emma"

kai: operational tip for rotations: create the new hosted key in Console (if you must), update it in the secrets store (Vault/GH Actions secrets), then restart consumers. Revoke old key after verifying consumers are using the new one. For local dev, rotate to a sandbox key instead.

emma: earlier I rotated and then my devbox still had the old value in ~/.env — that caused 401s. So update the secrets and reload envs, got it. Thanks.

leah: security reminder: do not commit hosted keys. If you accidentally push one, rotate immediately and open a security ticket. Our scanners will also flag commits and create an automated incident.

infra-bot: :warning: Policy: Hosted API keys are confidential. If a hosted key is exposed, rotate it and notify security@redwood.ai. Automated repo scanners may revoke/flag the key.

emma: one more edge case: I'm streaming responses and got a 429 mid-stream. Is that normal?

kai: yes, streaming still counts tokens in-flight — if you exceed quota mid-stream you'll get a 429. For long streams in dev, lower max_tokens or use a staging key. Also split long generation into smaller calls during tests.

leah: quick checklist for new hires hitting this: 1) use sandbox key for local dev, 2) don't commit keys, 3) implement retry with exponential backoff + jitter, 4) monitor X-RateLimit-* headers, 5) request CI sandbox key via #devex with the template, 6) rotate hosted keys by updating Console -> secrets store -> restart consumers -> revoke old key.

emma: saved. I'll open the devex request with the template for a 48h CI sandbox key. Appreciate the help! :thumbsup:
